title: refuses the placeholder team, and anything that is not a team, before anything runs
why: The team never checked: a build is judged against TEAMID_TBD, and every failure reads as a signing fault instead of a Team ID nobody wrote in.

title: is ten capital letters and digits, and never the placeholder
why: The placeholder with no sentence of its own: it is refused as a malformed Team ID, which does not say where the real one goes.

find: if (display.signature === 'adhoc') problems.push('it is signed ad hoc, not with a Developer ID')
title: passes the team's Developer ID build and names what an ad-hoc one is not
why: An ad-hoc signature not named as one: a signing-mode build that fell back to ad hoc fails on its consequences without the cause.

title: refuses another team's certificate, a development one, no timestamp and no runtime
why: TeamIdentifier not held to the team: a build signed by any Developer ID passes as this project's.

title: refuses another team's certificate, a development one, no timestamp and no runtime
why: A signature with no secure timestamp passed: the notary refuses it an hour later, and the disk image's own timestamp is the one thing only this check reads.

title: passes an ad-hoc build and names what a Developer ID one is not
why: The ad-hoc mark not required in adhoc mode: a branch build that picked up a certificate from somewhere passes as an ordinary one.

title: must set library validation off, as true, by its whole name
why: The entitlement never looked for: a build without disable-library-validation ships, and a person can no longer replace Electron's FFmpeg library (ADR-043).

title: fails on any override line, whatever else the verdict says
why: An overridden verdict taken as Gatekeeper's: on a machine with assessments off everything is accepted, signed or not.

title: passes only accepted, Notarized Developer ID, from the team
why: The source not read: an image that is signed and not notarised is accepted here and refused on a person's Mac.

title: fails when Gatekeeper is turned off, overridden, or names another team
why: Assessments turned off read as on: every verdict after it is a setting of the machine's, not a judgement of the build.

title: adds up to a worst case that is the sum of what each mode runs
why: A call left out of the worst case: a step limit set just past it stops the script before it can say which check hung.

title: imports nothing but Node's own modules: it runs on the runner that holds the notary's key
why: An import that is not node: let through: the next one can be a package, on the runner that holds the notary's key and installs none.
